chunks: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man wrote [a document for] the divorce of his wife or the emancipation of his slave, then he changed his mind and erased it.'
He said: 'That is not a divorce nor an emancipation until he speaks it.'

key_terms.بَدَا لَهُ: He changed his mind / it appeared otherwise — a standard legal phrase for retraction of intent
key_terms.طَلَاق: Divorce — the unilateral dissolution of marriage by the husband through a prescribed formula
key_terms.عِتْق / عَتَاق: Emancipation/manumission — the legal freeing of an enslaved person, a unilateral act requiring specific conditions
key_terms.يَتَكَلَّمَ بِهِ: He speaks it — verbal utterance as the constitutive act for legal validity

ai.seo_question: Does writing a divorce document count as divorce in Islamic law if it is later erased?
ai.summary: Zurara asked Imam al-Baqir (AS) about a man who wrote a divorce document or an emancipation document for his slave but then had a change of heart and erased what he had written. The Imam ruled that mere writing does not constitute a valid divorce or emancipation — the act only becomes legally effective when spoken aloud. This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that unilateral declarative acts (talaq and itq) require verbal utterance to take legal effect, and that a written document that is subsequently destroyed carries no consequence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, or Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara who said, 
‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man wrote with a divorce to his wife, or with an emancipation (liberation) of his clave. Then he changed his mind for it, so he deleted it’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not with a divorce nor an emancipation, until he speaks with it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa or ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife in writing or sets free his slave; he then changes his mind and deletes it.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not a divorce or setting free of a slave until he pronounces it through his mouth.’”
